spectra.caption: Plan your visit. The bar under the headline is today's opening hours, and the dot shows where you are in the day right now.
Getting here, as one scroll-driven trip: the plane lands, the metro brakes into Thaltej Gam, a taxi does the last 2 km, and the building lights up.
About. The building is the prism: a white beam hits it and splits into art, science, technology, your senses and you. Move the cursor and the light bends.

shivasva.caption: A section of the home page. The design is the client's; the backend, CMS and deployment behind it are mine.
Projects like Shivdhara Swarnim come out of the admin CMS. The client adds and edits their own projects, without calling me.
Brahmdhara Residency, another project. Each one is run from the same CMS, with its own pictures, address and details.
The contact form. You pick what the enquiry is about, and it goes to the client's email and into a Google Sheet.

sorted.caption: Client pick on a product shoot: 300 picked from 3,424 photos across 56 products. Every product gets its own row, so picking for a client is a scroll, not a folder hunt.
The products view. Every shot of the same product is grouped together, with how many photos and angles it has.
Every number on the site was measured on one machine, a 2020 MacBook Air with the base M1. 3,677 photos off one camera were searchable in 10 minutes 42 seconds.
From the shoot disk to the client's Drive the same night. Pick a person or a category, paste the client's Drive folder link, and it uploads straight from the SSD.
Between the disk and the delivery there are five steps: plug in, index, search, people, export. The disk is only read, never written to, and nothing leaves the Mac until you export.

cravache.caption: A brief lands on the desk, from a khaman house this time, with its fee, its patience and what it will cost you in sleep. You run the whole agency from screens like this one.

deepdive.caption: The Instagram page, followed by 150K+ marketers, founders and operators. The posts are found, written, designed and published by one server on a fixed schedule.
The blog opens on a rolling preview of the Instagram page, so a reader can go from the long reads to the reels in one click.
One long read a day on why an ad worked. It is written and published without me touching it.
Older posts stack up underneath, each with its own picture, date and read time.

vibe-raas-led.caption: One of the eight visuals. It is drawn live, not a video on loop, and it moves with the music because the software listens to the mixer.
The patterns are drawn from Gujarati textile and folk motifs and built by hand, eight visuals in four colourways.
A wide wall layout. One laptop drives all three walls, the 50 ft stage screen and the two side screens, and it works with no internet.
The control app on a phone. Pick the screens, the visual and the colours; the BPM comes off the mixer.

vibe-raas-tickets.caption: A pass as the buyer gets it: the night, the venue, how many passes, and a QR code to show at the gate.
A smaller order, with food. The seller typed the sale into Telegram the way they would say it, and this came back.

clapper.caption: The landing page at clapper.in, scrolled top to bottom: the hero, the shot log writing itself, how it works, and the free guides for whoever holds the phone on set.
